items.body:
### ESLint version

`main`

### What problem do you want to solve?

Right now, ESLint repositories intentionally do not check in package lockfiles such as `package-lock.json`. They instead have developers always install the latest matching version of packages specified in `package.json`s. The pros of this approach are:

* Recency: It forces developers onto the latest matching versions, which surfaces bugs / build breaks quickly
* Simplicity: one less root-level file in repositories

However, there are several drawbacks:

* Predictability: different machines can have different `node_modules/` structures based on when the install command was run
  * This can result in build breaks on `main` when an upstream package changes (see table in https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/20159#issuecomment-3389755576)
* Security: if a compromised package publishes a new patch version, because ESLint `package.json`s use `^` ranges, developers will start pulling it in

The predictability point in particular I find troublesome. Not having fully deterministic, predictable installs across machines makes for uncertainty.

### What do you think is the correct solution?

Two primary reasons, paraphrasing https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/20159#issuecomment-3334291476 & https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/20159#issuecomment-3517368062:

* Lockfiles solve those two issues
* Lockfiles are a standard practice for the npm ecosystem

Backing up the "standard practice" claim is this note from https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/configuring-npm/package-lock-json: _"This file is intended to be committed into source repositories"_. Furthermore, quick queries for file existence on Sourcegraph search:

* [`package-lock.json`: 175,700 results](https://sourcegraph.com/search?q=context:global+file:package-lock.json+count:900000&patternType=keyword&sm=0)
* [`npm-shrinkwrap.json`: 1.7k results](https://sourcegraph.com/search?q=context:global+file:npm-shrinkwrap.json&patternType=keyword&sm=0)

The following "create a new package" templates all create lockfiles:

* Angular: [`ng new`](https://angular.dev/tools/cli/setup-local)
* Expo: [`create-expo-app`](https://docs.expo.dev/more/create-expo)
* Nest.js: [`nest new`](https://docs.nestjs.com/cli/overview#basic-workflow)
* Next.js: [`create-next-app`](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/cli/create-next-app)
* Nuxt: [`create-nuxt`](https://nuxt.com/docs/4.x/getting-started/installation#new-project)
* Nx: [`create-nx-workspace`](https://nx.dev/docs/getting-started/start-new-project)
* Svelte: [`sv create`](https://svelte.dev/docs/kit/creating-a-project)
* Turbo: [`create-turbo`](https://turborepo.com/docs/getting-started/examples)
* TypeScript (community): [`create-typescript-app`](https://github.com/JoshuaKGoldberg/create-typescript-app) _(disclaimer: I'm the sole maintainer)_
* Vite: [`create-vite`](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/tree/main/packages/create-vite)

I believe it's somewhat unexpected, perhaps bordering on "weird", to not have a lockfile now.

---

https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/20159#issuecomment-3382017090 noted that:

> Adding `package-lock.json` without npm-shrinkwrap.json means we, and CI, would not be getting the same experience as end users. That can make it more difficult to to track problems down.

There is no one "experience" to be the same as. End users –with and without lockfiles- are all using different version ranges based on when they installed. 

For the goal of remaining up-to-date -which is a good one I agree with- repos generally use Dependabot or Renovate as ESLint does. A frequent cadence of version bump PRs ensures:

* The repository stays up-to-date with the latest in a predictable, trackable way
* Any breakages that users would experience are caught as they come in

### Participation

- [x] I am willing to submit a pull request for this change.

### Additional comments

#20159 was a large discussion originally around pinning dependencies in the context of supply chain security. It ballooned into discussing multiple separate areas of remediations:

* Internal: using lockfiles for established dependencies
* User-facing: switching from semver _ranges_ (e.g. `^`s) to specific _pinned_ versions

#20159 was closed for inactivity without resolution on either of those points. The idea of using `npm-shrinkwrap.json` files was brought up too as those are user-facing and not just internal. My intent for this issue is to avoid suggesting user-facing changes, and focus on the internal side. If the team wants to add user-facing remediations such as a shrinkwrap file and/or pinned versions, previously added lockfiles won't block that.

### Docs page(s)

https://eslint.org/docs/latest/rules/class-methods-use-this

### What documentation issue do you want to solve?

The docs for `class-methods-use-this` do a good job of explaining how to use the rule itself. But they don't include or link to any explanation of _why_ you'd want to use it. 

The docs also only suggest switching to a static function. That's not the only suggestible remediation. Oftentimes folks find standalone function declarations not associated with classes to be less overhead.

### What do you think is the correct solution?

Perhaps the rule docs could have a section explaining something like:

1. Upsides of using classes: encapsulation of state; reusability of logic; ...
2. The downside of taking that overhead on when encapsulation & reusability can be done with lighter-weight constructs: e.g. standalone functions
3. How class methods without `this` can be a sign of those downsides
4. 1-2 examples of refactors  

If there was a great canonical resource on why many _(not all)_ JavaScript programmers don't use classes, I would say we could at least link it there under _Further Reading_. I don't know of a great one.

### Participation

- [x] I am willing to submit a pull request for this change.

### Additional comments

This is a fraught area to document. I don't want to suggest advising against classes at all. But I do want to suggest the page explains the reasons for and against enabling the rule.

This came out of a conversation on Bluesky: https://bsky.app/profile/joshuakgoldberg.com/post/3lrj3elwbc22b

### What rule do you want to change?

func-style

### What change do you want to make?

Generate fewer warnings

### How do you think the change should be implemented?

A new default behavior

### Example code

```js
/* eslint func-style: "error" */

// func-style report: Expected a function expression.
function noOverloads() {}

// No func-style report
function hasOverloads(value: string): string
function hasOverloads(value: number): number
function hasOverloads(value: unknown) {
  return value;
}
```

### What does the rule currently do for this code?

```plaintext
Expected a function expression. 9:1 - 11:2
```

### What will the rule do after it's changed?

Not report on the function declaration.

### Participation

- [x] I am willing to submit a pull request to implement this change.

### Additional comments

Quoting https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/19719#issuecomment-2880017202:

> I would take [JoshuaKGoldberg's suggestion](https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/19719#issuecomment-2876875662) a step further and always allow overloaded function declarations. Don’t even add the option to report it. Otherwise it’s simply a TypeScript error.
> 
> [Playground](https://www.typescriptlang.org/play/?#code/GYVwdgxgLglg9mABACwIYGcDyA3ApgJwBs5UATdACm1UJFwC5F0p8YwBzASkedY4FgAUKEiwEKDDgLEylarQaIwIALYAjAtyWqN+IdXwSseIiXKIAvIhHR4YKjTqNwAazBwA7mE6IA3kMREfFwoEHwkeToAbiEAXyA)
> 
> ```ts
> function hasOverloads(value: string): string
> function hasOverloads(value: number): number
> var hasOverloads = function(value: unknown) {
>   return value;
> }
> ```
>
> If there’s user demand, there could be a rule to disallow TypeScript function overloads. But IMO that feels out of scope for `func-style`.

#19134 is an example of an issue where a change was merged into ESLint's `main` branch that caused downstream breakages in third-party plugins. Two popular examples: unicorn (https://github.com/sindresorhus/eslint-plugin-unicorn/issues/2496) and typescript-eslint (https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/issues/10338). The specific breaking PR was #17656 (by me, sorry folks 🙂). 

Proposal: how about we add some kind of ecosystem test to CI that runs some basic linting with these popular plugins? That way #17656's breakage would have been caught before hitting users.

To start, maybe targeting popular plugins with a lot of rules would be helpful for finding edge cases:
* [`eslint-plugin-unicorn`](https://github.com/sindresorhus/eslint-plugin-unicorn): for miscellaneous rules
* [`typescript-eslint`](https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint): for the TypeScript side
* [`eslint-plugin-vue`](https://github.com/vuejs/eslint-plugin-vue): for the framework side

If this is too heavyweight to put into individual PRs, it could alternately put only on the `main` branch. That way breakages would be discovered before a release.

For reference, we have some tests in typescript-eslint for community plugins that alert us when there's a breakage: e.g. https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/issues/10322 -> https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/pull/10328. 

Co-authored-by: @kirkwaiblinger

items.body:
When running `npx eslint` on a repository with many errors containing long descriptions and rule names, the stylish formatter can take a surprisingly long time to print results. @johnsoncodehk and I discovered this on https://github.com/johnsoncodehk/core/tree/d47d660758485c04dc26948b6ee9a42ac51a50df: more than half the command's time is spent in `printResults`! The problem is a very slow `/\s+$/` regex inside [`text-table`](https://unpkg.com/browse/text-table@0.2.0/index.js) on line 53. That regex is meant to remove all trailing whitespace in the string... which is now what [`String.prototype.trimEnd`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/String/trimEnd) does. The following fix inside `text-table` reduces the stylish formatter's runtime to near-zero: ```diff return map(row, function (c, ix) { // ... - }).join(hsep).replace(/\s+$/, ''); + }).join(hsep).trimEnd(); }).join('\n'); ``` Single example `time node node_modules/eslint/bin/eslint.js` measurements on my M1 Max Mac Studio, with screenshots of the equivalent attached `node --cpu-prof` traces:
Measurement time Trace
Baseline 17.35s
Fixed 8.70s
* [Baseline with replace regex.cpuprofile](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16337429/Baseline.with.replace.regex.cpuprofile) * [Fixed with string trimEnd.cpuprofile](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16337428/Fixed.with.string.trimEnd.cpuprofile)
Here is one of the strings being trimmed... ```js ' 972 5 \x1B[33mwarning\x1B[39m Unexpected nullable string value in conditional. Please handle the nullish/empty cases explicitly \x1B[2m@typescript-eslint/strict-boolean-expressions\x1B[22m ' ```
The stylish formatter calls to `text-table` here: https://github.com/eslint/eslint/blob/aab1b840f9cffb2a76a5c9fe1852961be71dc184/lib/cli-engine/formatters/stylish.js#L52 Coincidentally, #18618 was filed last month to suggest replacing the not-updated-for-11-years `text-table` dependency. It was closed for lack of motivation. @jonkoops, I imagine this issue might help you feel vindicated a bit? 😄 I went ahead and published a [`text-table-fast`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/text-table-fast) package that has roughly the same API as `text-table`, but without the quadratic regular expression or support for the `'.'` alignment (which ESLint doesn't use). Alternately, per https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/18618#issuecomment-2188553122, maybe it'd make sense to extract the useful bits of `text-table` into stylish itself, and get rid of some overhead? Co-authored-by: @johnsoncodehk

### ESLint version

8.57.0

### What problem do you want to solve?

Right now, nothing in ESLint core stops [inline configs (configuration comments)](https://eslint.org/docs/latest/use/configure/rules#using-configuration-comments) from redundantly repeating the same configuration _option_ and/or _severity_ as already exists. This is similar to [unused disable directives](https://eslint.org/docs/latest/use/configure/rules#report-unused-eslint-disable-comments): they take up space and can be misleading.

* [Playground of an inline config setting the same severity as the config file](https://eslint.org/play/#)
* [Playground of an inline config setting the same options as the config file](https://eslint.org/play/#)

### What do you think is the correct solution?

The most straightforward change I can think of would be to add a new `--report-unused-inline-configs` / `reportUnusedInlineConfigs` (per the feature's primary naming in #18187) or `--report-unused-config-comments` / `reportUnusedConfigComments` (per the common alternate naming).

### Participation

- [X] I am willing to submit a pull request for this change.

### Additional comments

Inspired by #18218, thanks @inga-lovinde 😄 

Edit: https://github.com/eslint/rfcs/pull/121 was filed and accepted for this.

### Docs page(s)

https://eslint.org/docs/latest/glossary

### What documentation issue do you want to solve?

There are a lot of terms around linting / ESLint that many users have trouble with:

* The difference between rule _"fixes"_ and _"suggestions"_ (https://github.com/eslint/eslint.org/issues/479)
* The specific terms used to describe types of rules: _"formatting"_, _"logical"_, and _"style"_ (https://github.com/eslint/eslint.org/issues/419)
* Terms relevant to linting or popular lint rules that many developers have trouble with: _"callback"_, _"expression"_, _"executor"_, _"identifier"_, _"scope"_, etc.
* Terms specific to linting (or contexts for existing terms): _"formatter"_, _"override"_, _"node"_, _"parser"_, _"plugin"_, _"report"_, _"rule"_, _"violation"_, ...really everything in the AST - and AST itself.

Many of those terms are explained within https://eslint.org/docs/latest/use right now, and especially within https://eslint.org/docs/latest/use/core-concepts. But those docs are written in long-form and meant to be consumed as a large entity. It's hard to find answers to a single _"what does '...' mean?"_ question within them.

### What do you think is the correct solution?

I'd love a dedicated _Glossary_ page in the site that succinctly describes what each of these terms mean & links to the docs that introduce each of them. That way, if someone asks what a term means, we can give them a more precise answer than a general docs page.

### Participation

- [X] I am willing to submit a pull request for this change.

### Additional comments

Other examples in the wild of "glossary" vs "use" splits in docs:
* https://codecademy.com/docs is an example of a general-purpose coding glossary
* https://react.dev has a split between "learn" and "reference"

### Docs page(s)

https://eslint.org/docs/latest/faqs

### What documentation issue do you want to solve?

Looking back through the [Discord `#help` channel](https://discord.com/channels/688543509199716507/1059928426217209896), at least two duplicate-ish requests keep popping up:

* `ESLint couldn't find the config "..." to extend from.`: 18 search results
* `ESLint couldn't determine the plugin "..." uniquely.`: 14 search results

This indicates to me that there are some questions people are continuously asking and don't know how to troubleshoot themselves.

### What do you think is the correct solution?

ESLint could shortcut answers to these common questions with a dedicated FAQs page linked in `#help` and those errors' messages. 

We've anecdotally had good results in typescript-eslint from [typescript-eslint.io > Troubleshooting & FAQs](https://typescript-eslint.io/linting/troubleshooting) helping reduce duplicate questions.

### Participation

- [X] I am willing to submit a pull request for this change.

### Additional comments

ESLint error messages right now end with:

```plaintext
If you still can't figure out the problem, please stop by https://eslint.org/chat/help to chat with the team.
```

I think that's why so many folks go straight to the `#help` channel in Discord. Perhaps having them go to an "Frequently Asked Questions" or "Troubleshooting and FAQs" page first would reduce the amount of clear duplicates in the channel? Or even if this issue is declined, perhaps directing them to read the docs first would be a good intermediate solution?

There is a [README.md Frequently Asked Questions](https://github.com/eslint/eslint/?tab=readme-ov-file#frequently-asked-questions) section right now. But:

* It's a mix of project-level items and actual debugging. The first question is on JSCS.
* It's not in the website, and many devs presumably aren't reading through the GitHub README.md.

### ESLint version

v8.56.0

### What problem do you want to solve?

Porting https://github.com/JoshuaKGoldberg/eslint-plugin-expect-type/issues/115 over to ESLint core: at least one community plugin -`eslint-plugin-expect-type` has a rule whose fixer operates on a separate "snapshot" file in the file system, _not_ the file being linted. That rule has no native way of knowing whether ESLint is being run in `--fix` mode. Because fixers run even if ESLint isn't in fix mode, the fixer can't reliably know whether it should update the file snapshot.

### What do you think is the correct solution?

~Two thoughts:~

* ~Can we avoid running `fix()` functions when not in fix mode?~
* ~Alternately, can a rule's `context` object contain info on whether the fixer is being run? Or the `fixer` passed to the `fix()` function?~

Edit (Jan 9): https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/17881#issuecomment-1883593657 shows the current proposal of enabling suggestions to specify changes to other files in limited cases:

> * Limiting this option to `suggestions`, not fixes?
> * Add a new `meta` property like `meta.allowSuggestingFileChanges` _(but with a better name)_?
> * Having these out-of-file changes go through `fixer` methods that limit the allowed actions in some way?

### Participation

- [X] I am willing to submit a pull request for this change.

### Additional comments

A rules equivalent of what I proposed a year ago in https://github.com/eslint/rfcs/pull/102, perhaps? 🙂 

Edit (Jan 9): Later comments have filled in use cases:

* [eslint-plugin-expect-type](https://github.com/JoshuaKGoldberg/eslint-plugin-expect-type)'s [expect-type/expect rule](https://github.com/JoshuaKGoldberg/eslint-plugin-expect-type/blob/ea67df6f3c90b94ac550b7c47f2579b4c18cc46f/docs/rules/expect.md)'s [$ExpectTypeSnapshot feature](https://github.com/JoshuaKGoldberg/eslint-plugin-expect-type/blob/ea67df6f3c90b94ac550b7c47f2579b4c18cc46f/docs/rules/expect.md#expecttypesnapshot) (https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/17881#issuecomment-1873507895)
* CSS-in-JS styling systems such as [Panda CSS](https://panda-css.com) and [Vanilla Extract](https://vanilla-extract.style) being able to suggest moving `css(...)` calls to a new file (https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/17881#issuecomment-1874772298)
* Spell-checkers such as the [cspell spellchecker](https://github.com/streetsidesoftware/cspell) project's [@cspell/eslint ESLint plugin](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@cspell/eslint-plugin) being able to suggest adding to a user dictionary (https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/17881#issuecomment-1883593657)

### ESLint version

N/A

### What problem do you want to solve?

Forgive me / feel free to close this issue if the answer to this inquiry hasn't changed. I couldn't find a dedicated issue for this discussion so I'm opening one here.

Obviously, prettier is popular in the ecosystem for automatic code formatting.

To date, we have not adopted prettier internally in the ESLint codebase because we want to dogfood our own formatting rules ([link to comment](https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/17504#issuecomment-1701291317)):

> > As a side note, I'd love to see our code formatted with Prettier as well, but there's likely a discussion on GitHub somewhere explaining why we haven't adopted it.
> 
> Dogfooding. It's a lot easier to find bugs in formatting rules if we use them exclusively.

However, I'm raising this issue due to some recent developments:

1. We're on the verge of formatting our markdown docs with prettier: https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/17504
2. We recently deprecated formatting rules: https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/17522
3. Formatting/stylistic rules have been frozen since 2020: https://eslint.org/blog/2020/05/changes-to-rules-policies/

### What do you think is the correct solution?

These developments could be an opening for us to adopt prettier internally in the ESLint codebase for JavaScript files, as it may be less important to dogfood our formatting rules when they are deprecated and frozen (as well as unit-tested like all rules) and we've already adopted prettier elsewhere. 

If now is not the time, then would we consider prettier at any of these future milestones?

1. When we remove formatting rules in a future major version.
2. During a future rewrite of ESLint.
3. Never.

The main downside of adopting prettier is that it would pollute the git blame history for virtually every line in the codebase, although it's possible to workaround that by listing the prettier adoption commit to be ignored in a `.git-blame-ignore-revs` file alongside `git blame --ignore-revs-file .git-blame-ignore-revs`.

### Participation

- [X] I am willing to submit a pull request for this change.

### Additional comments

### ESLint version

HEAD

### What problem do you want to solve?

We currently ship 12 formatters in the core of ESLint. This was helpful early on to get people started with ESLint and help them transition from existing tools. However, the results of the user survey show very few people use anything but the default formatter (stylish). 

Additionally, the `tap` formatter requires the `js-yaml` package, which isn't need anywhere else in the core, so removing this would mean eliminating a dependency. (Eventually -- `@eslint/eslintrc` also depends on `js-yaml`, but that dependency will be removed in v10.)

### What do you think is the correct solution?

Remove all of the formatters except stylish, json, and json-with-meta. Almost all of the remaining formatters have already been published as their own packages: https://github.com/fregante/eslint-formatters. We can advise people to use those packages if they need to continue using one of these formatters.

### Participation

- [X] I am willing to submit a pull request for this change.

### Additional comments

Maybe we'd also like to keep `html`? It looks like `eslint-formatter-html` already exists and isn't the code that we have.

### ESLint version

v8.46.0

### What problem do you want to solve?

Right now, there's no programmatic way to determine what any given rule's default options are. Many rules define functions like `normalizeOptions` ([`array-bracket-newline`](https://github.com/eslint/eslint/blob/e52b98bf25d882da4efd5559ce5974b6697cf701/lib/rules/array-bracket-newline.js#L102)), [`array-element-newline`](https://github.com/eslint/eslint/blob/e52b98bf25d882da4efd5559ce5974b6697cf701/lib/rules/array-element-newline.js#L120), [`object-curly-newline`](https://github.com/eslint/eslint/blob/e52b98bf25d882da4efd5559ce5974b6697cf701/lib/rules/object-curly-newline.js#L99)) or `parseOptions` ([`no-implicit-coercion`](https://github.com/eslint/eslint/blob/e52b98bf25d882da4efd5559ce5974b6697cf701/lib/rules/no-implicit-coercion.js#L22), [`use-before-define`](https://github.com/eslint/eslint/blob/e52b98bf25d882da4efd5559ce5974b6697cf701/lib/rules/no-use-before-define.js#L20)) that apply various, subtly different value defaults.

As a result, the only user-facing way to determine a rule's default options is to read the docs. But the docs themselves aren't consistent in phrasing. For example:
* [`array-callback-return`](https://eslint.org/docs/latest/rules/array-callback-return#options) phrases its options as _`"<key>": <value> (default) <explanation>`_
* [`accessor-pairs`](https://eslint.org/docs/latest/rules/accessor-pairs#options) phrases its options as _`<key> <explanation> (Default <default>)`_

Furthermore, there's also no way for tooling to determine the default options for any rule. Which is making it hard for us in typescript-eslint to automate our docs pages for extended rules (https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/issues/6841#issuecomment-1668497510).

### What do you think is the correct solution?

In typescript-eslint, we added a `defaultOptions` property on rules. It's visible in the [Custom Rules guide](https://typescript-eslint.io/developers/custom-rules#rulecreator), which suggests users wrap rule creation with a `createRule`:

```ts
import { ESLintUtils } from '@typescript-eslint/utils';

const createRule = ESLintUtils.RuleCreator(
  name => `https://example.com/rule/${name}`,
);

export const rule = createRule({
  create(context) { /* ... */ },
  defaultOptions: [ { /* ... */ } ],
  meta: { /* ... */ },
  name: "..."
});
```

Under the hood, `createRule` wraps `create` to fill in `defaultOptions` for any option not provided by the ESLint config. You can see the exact logic here: https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/blob/9c17395d7cd6da7e2db59f9bde2c81264a33da97/packages/utils/src/eslint-utils/applyDefault.ts. It's a deep merge, not a shallow `Object.assign`.

Would ESLint core be interested in adding an equivalent to this logic? And/or, would you like an RFC written for it?

### Participation

- [X] I am willing to submit a pull request for this change.

### Additional comments

I don't believe this would be a breaking change the way #14709 is. Making the new field optional means rules can opt into it if they please.

### ESLint version

v8.29.0

### What problem do you want to solve?

Forking from https://github.com/eslint/eslint/discussions/16557#discussioncomment-4219483: custom parsers sometimes would want to make decisions based on the way ESLint is being run. For example, [`@typescript-eslint/parser`](https://typescript-eslint.io)'s [type-aware linting mode](https://typescript-eslint.io/docs/linting/typed-linting):

* Has to use not-always-correct inferences to know whether to use an _immutable_ TypeScript program (faster but can't react to file changes) or a _builder_ TypeScript program (slower but can react to file changes).
* Can't create file watchers on disk because we don't know when the lint program is done.
    * Given file A importing from file B, we can't inform file A when file B's exported types are changed. This results in frequent user pain: https://typescript-eslint.io/linting/troubleshooting#changes-to-one-file-are-not-reflected-when-linting-other-files-in-my-ide

One piece of information that would really help us out on the parser side would be to know ESLint's runtime mode:

* "One and done" runs: which can have a reusable (_immutable_ program) cache, and doesn't need to attach file watchers
* "One and done, with fixers": which have a _mostly_ reusable cache, except for file fixes, which we generally assume not to change cross-file types
* "Continuous" runs: the "wild west" (_builder_ program), and should attach file watchers

From knowing the usage mode, parsers can then make more informed decision on aspects such as file/program caching. https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/pull/6178 shows an example of typescript-eslint using this information to determine whether it's in a "single run" mode _without_ `--fix`. That "single run" mode helps with performance (https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/pull/3512 -> https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/issues/3528) but has issues when `--fix` is enabled (https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/issues/6176 -> https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/issues/6184).

### What do you think is the correct solution?

I'd like to suggest we provide a `session` object to parsers that at first contains just two pieces of information:

```ts
interface LintSession {
  mode?: "persistent" | "single";
  options: ESLintOptions;
}
```

The expectation for this session object is that consumers may provide a `mode` _if_ they know it:

- [`CLIEngine`](https://eslint.org/docs/latest/developer-guide/architecture/#the-cliengine-object) would always provide `mode: 'single'`
- [`Linter`](https://eslint.org/docs/latest/developer-guide/architecture/#the-linter-object) would receive an optional mode from whoever is constructing & using it

Parsers would then receive the session in their [`parseForESLint`](https://eslint.org/docs/latest/developer-guide/working-with-custom-parsers) as a third parameter.


### Participation

- [X] I am willing to submit a pull request for this change.

### Additional comments

This feels meaty enough to become an RFC. But the RFC README.md seems to suggest posting an issue first. 🙂 

Other fields could eventually be added to session (I'd really love to have file watching handles, to make addressing the issues with watching even more straightforward to resolve). But in the hope of getting this merged in sooner, I'm leaving them out of this proposal for now.

By _✔️  I am willing to submit a pull request for this change._ I mean - I would experience _great_ personal & professional joy in implementing this. Please let me do this thing! 😁 

I'd chatted with @bradzacher and @ljharb briefly about this before filing but haven't gone through much bikeshedding on the contents or naming of that session object.
